title: The Patternmaker Behind the Designer
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: The patternmaker is not a neutral copying machine: pattern work carries design intention into geometry, fit, construction, repeatability, and the body through skilled decisions that deserve explicit evidence, authority, and credit.
Construction evidence can outlive the operating house—but only if the physical object and record stay paired.

01 · BRIEF — What is the design asking the pattern to do?. Record silhouette, balance, ease, movement, material behavior, size range, construction, finish, cost, time, accessibility, and the non-negotiable visual idea. A sketch alone rarely carries all of this.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · JUDGMENT — Which decisions belong to the patternmaker?. Log the alteration, reason, evidence, person deciding, person approving, affected sizes and materials, and whether the change is technical, aesthetic, safety-related, or commercial. Skilled translation should remain attributable.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · FIT — Whose body becomes the standard?. Identify the block, fit model or measurement source, sample size, grading method, movement test, wearer feedback, and excluded bodies. A technically repeatable pattern can still institutionalize a narrow body assumption.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · RETAIN — Can the knowledge survive the specialist’s absence?. Preserve pattern version, annotation, toile images where permitted, fitting decisions, known failures, material constraints, maker credit, access rules, and a route for future questions. The file is evidence; narration explains the judgment.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Select one garment and pair the approved sketch, first pattern, first toile, fitting record, production pattern, and final object.
Interview the patternmaker about three changes that are invisible in the finished photograph.
Record who proposed, tested, approved, rejected, and documented each change.
Audit fit assumptions, size coverage, credit, compensation, file custody, reuse, and succession with the actual participants.
